architecture: Benchtop conveyor testbed with 1.2 m synthetic belt loop, brushless DC motor, piezo accelerometer on idler bearing housing, and ultrasonic acoustic sensor clamped to belt surface guide.
hypothesis: An artificial surface defect produces periodic ultrasonic bursts (>25 kHz) synchronized with belt circulation (T = L / V), distinguishable from roller speed-dependent baseline noise.
independent_variables: Defect presence (baseline vs 1 mm artificial notch)
controlled_variables: Acoustic sensor clamp force (5 N with silicone couplant)
equipment: 1.2 m benchtop conveyor rig with variable speed DC drive
High-frequency contact acoustic emission sensor (20-100 kHz)
Removable artificial notch test fixture (1 mm notch)
calibration: Zero sensors at standstill (record stationary noise floor).
Calibrate accelerometer mounting torque to 2.5 Nm using torque wrench.
Verify acoustic sensor couplant contact pressure with 5 N clamp gauge.
protocol: 1. Power on DAQ and initiate background noise logging for 10 seconds at 0 m/s.
2. Run baseline condition without defect at 1.0 m/s for 30 seconds; log channels.
3. Run baseline condition without defect at 2.0 m/s for 30 seconds; log channels.
4. Stop motor, install 1 mm artificial defect clip at marker position on belt.
5. Run defect condition at 1.0 m/s for 30 seconds; log channels.
6. Run defect condition at 2.0 m/s for 30 seconds; log channels.
7. Export raw data to data_template.csv and execute analysis.py.
measurement_plan: Record time-series at 250 kS/s. Extract peak acoustic amplitude and burst repetition frequency. Calculate descriptive statistics (mean, std dev, min, max) for each trial condition.
sample_size_rationale: 5 continuous belt cycles per condition (30 seconds per run at 1-2 m/s provides 25-50 cycles), sufficient for descriptive signal-to-noise ratio assessment.
acceptance_criteria: Supports hypothesis if: Periodic acoustic burst amplitude exceeds baseline mean by >=6 dB and burst period matches T = 1.2m / V across both 1.0 m/s and 2.0 m/s.
Weakens hypothesis if: Acoustic amplitude does not exceed baseline noise floor, or amplitude scales only with speed regardless of defect presence.
Inconclusive if: Signal-to-noise ratio is below 6 dB or sensor mounting slips during run.
safety: Benchtop safety shield must be closed during belt operation.
Emergency stop button within immediate operator reach.
Keep hands and loose clothing clear of rotating rollers and nip points.
